stories.title: Citi Provides $210M Refi for Grand Hyatt Resort in Southern California
stories.excerpt: Citi has provided $210 million in refinancing for Trinity Investments’ 531-key luxury hotel in Southern California’s Coachella Valley. JLL Capital Markets arranged the five-year, floating-rate, single-asset, single-borrower commercial mortgage-backed securities loan for the Grand Hyatt Indian Wells Resort & Villas. The financing comes after a $62 million renovation and conversion of the property to the Grand Hyatt brand in 2024. The 45-acre resort is at 44600 Indian Wells Lane in Indian Wells in Riverside County, about 20 miles southeast of Palm Springs. The property features 449 guestrooms, 39 suites and 43 villas, as well as more than 88,000 square feet of indoor and outdoor meeting and event space. The resort also includes nine swimming pools, a water park, a 30,000-square-foot spa, six restaurants and bars, and tennis and pickleball courts. Kevin Davis, Americas CEO of JLL’s hotels and hospitality group, said that recently renovated resorts are attracting more lenders. “The hospitality financing market has shown meaningful momentum this year, with lenders focusing capital on repositioned assets with institutional sponsorship in markets where supply constraints support sustained performance,” Davis said in a statement. JLL’s Mike Huth and Jade Lewin arranged the financing with Davis. Miami-based Trinity specializes in acquiring, repositioning and operating hotels and resorts, and has deployed more than $10 billion across the United States, Mexico, Europe and Japan. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Citi provides $210M CMBS refi for 531-key Grand Hyatt Indian Wells, Coachella Valley.
Property underwent $62M renovation, conversion to Grand Hyatt brand in 2024.
45-acre resort features 449 rooms, 39 suites, 43 villas, 88k SF event space.
stories.summary: Citi arranged a $210 million five-year floating-rate CMBS loan for Trinity Investments' 531-key Grand Hyatt Indian Wells Resort & Villas in Riverside County, California. The property recently completed a $62 million renovation and brand conversion in 2024. The 45-acre resort includes 449 guestrooms, 39 suites, 43 villas, nine pools, a 30,000-square-foot spa, and extensive meeting and amenity space.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. Signals strong lender appetite for recently repositioned hospitality assets, but does not indicate demand or capital flows affecting apartment markets. The financing availability may suggest moderately improved CMBS conditions, though hospitality assets carry different risk profiles than residential.

stories.title: L.A. Industrial Vacancy Falls for First Time in Two Years
stories.excerpt: Los Angeles County’s industrial real estate market extended its recovery over the summer with its fourth quarter in a row of positive net absorption and its first annual decline in vacancy in at least two years. A new report from CBRE shows industrial tenants absorbed 1.9 million square feet during the third quarter, compared with negative 2.4 million square feet during the same period a year earlier. The market has had 5.1 million square feet of absorption since the start of the year, following more than two years of quarterly losses between mid-2023 and late 2025. The vacancy rate fell 20 basis points from both the second quarter and a year earlier to 5 percent, while leasing activity reached 13.7 million square feet, up 6.5 percent year-over-year. However, leasing volume declined 15.7 percent from the second quarter. Demand was particularly strong for larger warehouses. Industrial buildings measuring at least 250,000 square feet accounted for almost 2.1 million square feet of positive absorption during the third quarter. Those properties represented about 96 percent of the space absorbed this year. Smaller industrial properties have struggled, however. Buildings smaller than 50,000 square feet recorded negative absorption of 320,000 square feet during the quarter and 1.43 million square feet through September. Despite improving occupancy, average direct asking rents held steady at $1.19 per square foot per month on a triple-net basis, following declines in 10 of the previous 11 quarters. That figure remains 4 percent below the average from a year ago, and 30.4 percent below the $1.71 per square foot recorded in the third quarter of 2023. Central L.A. led the county with 1.11 million square feet of positive absorption, followed by the South Bay with 488,000 square feet and the San Gabriel Valley with 442,000 square feet. bullets: LA County industrial vacancy fell to 5%, down 20 bps YoY; first annual decline in 2+ years.
Market absorbed 5.1M SF YTD after 2+ years of quarterly losses; 1.9M SF in Q3.
Large warehouses (250k+ SF) drove 2.1M SF absorption in Q3; leasing volume 13.7M SF.
stories.summary: Los Angeles County's industrial market posted its first annual vacancy decline in at least two years, with the rate falling to 5% in Q3 2024. The market absorbed 1.9 million square feet during Q3 and 5.1 million square feet YTD, reversing more than two years of quarterly losses. Leasing activity reached 13.7 million square feet, up 6.5% year-over-year, with particularly strong demand for large warehouses exceeding 250,000 square feet.
stories.impact: Industrial recovery signals potential reduced speculative multifamily demand in LA; strong warehouse leasing may indicate e-commerce logistics expansion and job growth in logistics/distribution roles. However, industrial and residential operate in separate markets with different land constraints, so cross-sector competition remains modest. Monitor whether warehouse job creation in LA suburbs (Hesperia, Inland Empire) drives downstream residential demand in those submarkets.

stories.title: Samsung to Add Second Fab to Taylor Facility
stories.excerpt: Samsung is looking to break ground on its second chip fab in Taylor, Texas, this November, with mass production targeted for 2030. The Taylor Fab 2 will span roughly 2.7 million square feet. The facility will be one and a half times bigger than Fab One. As an illustration, the Austin Business Journal reports the production footprint will equate to the size of nine football fields – larger than the first building, which is the equivalent of six football fields. The first Taylor fab has operations planned by the end of 2026 and volume production in 2027. Its best-known customer is Tesla, which signed a $16.5 billion deal running through 2033. Samsung plans to invest over $37 billion across Central Texas, backed by up to $4.745 billion in CHIPS Act funding. The post Samsung to Add Second Fab to Taylor Facility appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Samsung breaks ground November on Fab 2 in Taylor, Texas; 2.7M SF, 1.5x larger than Fab 1.
Mass production targeted 2030; Samsung investing $37B across Central Texas with $4.745B CHIPS Act funding.
Fab 1 targets operations end of 2026, volume production 2027; Tesla customer ($16.5B deal through 2033).
stories.summary: Samsung is set to begin construction in November on its second fab facility in Taylor, Texas, a 2.7 million-square-foot plant targeting mass production in 2030. The Fab 2 will be 1.5 times larger than Fab 1, which aims for operations by end of 2026. Samsung plans to invest over $37 billion across Central Texas, backed by up to $4.745 billion in CHIPS Act funding, with major customer Tesla secured through a $16.5 billion deal running through 2033.
stories.impact: Massive employment multiplier for Austin-Taylor metros: semiconductor fabs employ highly-skilled workers (engineers, technicians, support staff) at premium wages, driving high-income household formation. Both fabs will generate 10,000+ direct and indirect jobs through 2030, creating sustained rental demand for Class A apartments near Taylor and Austin tech corridors. Developers should prioritize acquisition and entitlements in Taylor and north Austin submarkets ahead of 2026–2027 job influx; anticipate 20–30% rent growth in proximate markets as skilled workforce in-migrates.

stories.title: Cushman & Wakefield Scores Marketing Deal for Two Houston City-Owned Towers
stories.excerpt: The Houston City Council passed an ordinance allowing the city to work with commercial real estate company Cushman & Wakefield to sell 611 Walker St. and 1200 Travis St., which house the Houston Public Works Department and the Houston Police Department, respectively. Both of those agencies will relocate to 1600 Smith St., which the city recently acquired. Community Impact reports that Houston Public Works says both buildings, built in 1966, have weak generators and outdated electrical systems. In July 2025, Macchi said that the HPW building had an 18% remaining service life and the HPD building was at 15% if the city does not make improvements. The city says it can’t afford to perform the improvements needed to keep them open. Cushman & Wakefield’s Tim Relyea is handling the sale of the properties on behalf of the city. Both properties are likely candidates for redevelopment. Offices, hotels and residential are all possibilities. The post Cushman & Wakefield Scores Marketing Deal for Two Houston City-Owned Towers appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Houston sells two city-owned 1966-built office towers: 611 Walker St. and 1200 Travis St.
Public Works and Police Departments relocate to 1600 Smith St.; buildings have 18% and 15% remaining service life.
Cushman & Wakefield marketing for sale; mixed-use redevelopment (office, hotel, residential) likely.
stories.summary: Houston City Council authorized Cushman & Wakefield to market and sell 611 Walker Street and 1200 Travis Street, two city-owned office towers built in 1966 that house the Public Works and Police Departments. Both buildings have severely degraded infrastructure (18% and 15% remaining service life, respectively) that the city cannot afford to repair. The agencies will relocate to 1600 Smith Street, and the properties are expected candidates for office, hotel, or residential redevelopment.
stories.impact: Significant redevelopment opportunity in downtown Houston: two prime downtown sites, approximately 500k+ SF combined, now entering market. Strong signal of downtown office distress and municipal exit, but twin towers' downtown location and potential mixed-use zoning support residential conversion. If residential redevelopment proceeds, this adds supply in Houston's CBD and may compete with or complement near-downtown apartment projects; monitor absorption and pricing in downtown/midtown Houston submarkets.

stories.title: Dallas’s The Knox, Auberge Collection Taking Reservations Starting at $1,000 a Night
stories.excerpt: The Knox, Auberge Collection is now accepting bookings for stays beginning January 29th. The new hotel is in the heart of Dallas’s Knox Street neighborhood. Rates start at $1,000. The Knox, Auberge Collection is made possible through a partnership with BDT & MSD Partners and its partner, Trammell Crow Company. The hotel will feature 140 guest rooms and suites, along with 48 premier private residences, complemented by a collection of signature dining experiences, a spa, and a pool garden with skyline views. The Knox, Auberge Collection offers two- and three-bedroom apartments designed for longer stays with expansive indoor-outdoor living, a kitchen-area, generous gathering spaces, and thoughtfully appointed interiors. The post Dallas’s The Knox, Auberge Collection Taking Reservations Starting at $1,000 a Night appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: The Knox, Auberge Collection opens January 29 in Dallas Knox Street neighborhood; rates start $1,000/night.
140 guest rooms/suites plus 48 premier private residences; 2–3 bed apartments for longer-stay guests.
Joint venture: BDT & MSD Partners and Trammell Crow Company; dining, spa, pool, skyline views.
stories.summary: The Knox, Auberge Collection, a luxury hotel and residences developed through partnership of BDT & MSD Partners and Trammell Crow Company, is now accepting reservations beginning January 29 in Dallas's Knox Street neighborhood at nightly rates starting at $1,000. The 140-room hotel features 48 premier private residences, including two- and three-bedroom apartments designed for extended stays with full kitchens and amenities including signature dining, spa, and skyline pool.
stories.impact: Signals strength of Dallas luxury residential market and Trammell Crow's appetite for high-end mixed-use/hospitality-residential hybrids in premium submarkets. The extended-stay apartment component embedded in a luxury hotel asset reflects hybrid demand (corporate relocations, extended TDY) and capital's confidence in Knox Street's upscale demographic. Monitor whether this model influences future Trammell Crow and peer development strategies for ultra-prime locations in major metros.

stories.title: AI is Making Power the New Driver of Real Estate Value, Say ULI and Heitman
stories.excerpt: The expanding use of artificial intelligence and development of data centers to generate it are making access to power the new driver of real estate value, the Urban Land Institute (ULI) and Heitman said in a new report. According to the report, titled Investment Strategies in the AI Era: Power Is the New Location, reliable access to power, transmission infrastructure and connectivity increasingly influences where development can occur and which markets attract investment. The report explores how artificial intelligence is reshaping real estate economics and redefining the drivers of long-term value creation. Markets with abundant energy, transmission capacity, fiber connectivity and the ability to deliver new power quickly could gain a growing advantage in attracting investment, development, jobs and economic activity. “For decades, the first rule of real estate was location, location, location,” said Laura Craft, global head of portfolio sustainability Strategies at Heitman. “As AI transforms the global economy, power availability is becoming just as important. Access to power, connectivity, and technology-ready infrastructure will increasingly shape where investment flows and where growth occurs.” The report also finds that AI’s influence on real estate opportunities extends beyond data centers. Powered land, battery storage, industrial facilities, workforce housing and distributed computing infrastructure could all benefit from AI-driven growth. The post AI is Making Power the New Driver of Real Estate Value, Say ULI and Heitman appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: ULI and Heitman report: AI, data centers redefine real estate; power now driver of location value.
Reliable power access, transmission capacity, fiber connectivity increasingly influence development feasibility and investment.
Markets with abundant energy and fast power delivery gain advantage in attracting investment, jobs, economic activity.
stories.summary: The Urban Land Institute and Heitman released a report titled "Investment Strategies in the AI Era: Power Is the New Location," arguing that reliable access to power, transmission infrastructure, and connectivity are becoming as critical as traditional location factors in real estate investment and development. Markets with abundant energy capacity, strong transmission infrastructure, and the ability to rapidly deploy new power will gain competitive advantage in attracting development, jobs, and capital. The report notes that AI's expansion is fundamentally reshaping real estate economics and long-term value creation drivers.
stories.impact: Structural shift in real estate site selection criteria favors markets with excess power generation and transmission capacity (TX, OK, regions with cheap hydroelectric power, etc.) and penalizes constrained, high-cost-power markets (CA, parts of Northeast). Multifamily developers should evaluate power grid stability and cost in underwriting; markets with affordable, reliable power will attract tech/data-center employment clusters, driving population in-migration and higher-income rental demand. Conversely, apartment projects in power-constrained metros face longer-term headwinds if regional job growth falters.

stories.title: Coors Family Mixed-Use Venture Completes First Phase
stories.excerpt: The first phase of Clayworks, a 14-acre, six-block redevelopment of the former CoorsTek ceramics manufacturing site in Golden, Colorado, is now complete with the opening of The Pottery, a new 188,600-square-foot office building developed by AC Development, the Coors family’s development company. CoorsTek and AC Development teams completed their move into The Pottery this month. The workplace gives CoorsTek employees a modern headquarters while maintaining the company’s longstanding connection to Golden. Additional office and retail space is currently available for lease within the building. Clayworks is transforming the former Coors industrial campus into a mixed-use neighborhood across six city blocks, with plans for office, retail, dining, public gathering areas, housing, parking and a future boutique hotel. The project will preserve elements of the property’s history while creating new spaces for the Golden community. Sweet Bloom Co The Pottery was created through the adaptive reuse of the former CoorsTek headquarters and manufacturing facilities,. The Pottery was developed by AC Development, with Tryba Architects serving as architect and Holder Construction as general contractor. The post Coors Family Mixed-Use Venture Completes First Phase appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Clayworks Phase 1 complete: The Pottery, 188.6k SF office building, Golden, Colorado redevelopment.
14-acre, six-block adaptive reuse of former CoorsTek ceramics site; CoorsTek headquarters now in building.
Planned six-block mixed-use: office, retail, dining, housing, hotel, parking, public gathering areas.
stories.summary: Clayworks, a 14-acre, six-block redevelopment of the former CoorsTek ceramics manufacturing site in Golden, Colorado, has completed Phase 1 with the opening of The Pottery, a 188,600-square-foot office building developed by AC Development (the Coors family's company). CoorsTek and AC Development teams moved into the space in 2024. The broader Clayworks project plans mixed-use development including office, retail, dining, housing, parking, a boutique hotel, and public gathering areas across the six city blocks.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance; project is office-anchor-driven mixed-use redevelopment, not apartment-first. However, signals family office and local capital appetite for mixed-use real estate; residential component may include market-rate apartments, offering secondary density/diversification. Monitor Golden, CO market for downstream multifamily demand driven by office employment and community activation, though scale is regional not metropolitan.

stories.title: Walker & Dunlop Investment Partners Supplies $63M Refi for Illinois Apartments
stories.excerpt: Noah Properties has landed $62.5 million of lease-up financing for a newly built multifamily development in suburban Chicago, Commercial Observer has learned. Walker & Dunlop Investment Partners (WDIP) originated the loan for 945 Nanusha Residences in Buffalo Grove, Ill. The deal refinances existing construction debt ahead of its temporary certificate of occupancy (TCO) , prior to the lease-up process. Arrow Real Estate Advisors negotiated the transaction with a team led by Morris Betesh and Jacob Petrovic. The refi was structured with an interest reserve through lease-up to finance remaining project costs and cover real estate tax and insurance expenses, according to Arrow. “WDIP stepped up on a pre-TCO takeout that materially reduces Noah’s cost of capital, carries the property all the way through stabilization on a single loan and closed in roughly 30 days from sign-up,” Petrovic, director at Arrow Real Estate Advisors, said in a statement. Betesh, founder and managing partner at Arrow, said Chicago and the Midwest have been “a core growth priority” for the brokerage this year, with 945 Nanusha Residences showcasing this conviction of “high-quality product in deep suburban submarkets.” Located at 945 North Old Arlington Heights Road around 30 miles northwest of Downtown Chicago, 945 Nanusha Residences consists of 223 apartments across 231,970 gross square feet. Resident amenities include a courtyard, a swimming pool, cabanas, an outdoor grilling area, a rooftop lounge with fire pit, a fitness center and electric vehicle charging stations. WDIP and Noah Properties did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Walker & Dunlop Investment Partners provides $62.5M lease-up financing for 945 Nanusha Residences, Buffalo Grove, Illinois.
Pre-TCO takeout refinances construction debt; interest reserve covers lease-up costs and operating expenses.
Loan closed in ~30 days; financing carries property through stabilization on single loan.
stories.summary: Noah Properties secured $62.5 million in lease-up financing from Walker & Dunlop Investment Partners for 945 Nanusha Residences, a newly built multifamily development in Buffalo Grove, Illinois (suburban Chicago). The loan refinances existing construction debt ahead of temporary certificate of occupancy and includes an interest reserve to cover remaining project costs and operating expenses through lease-up. The transaction closed in approximately 30 days.
stories.impact: Signals strong lender appetite for newly delivered multifamily in Chicago suburbs; pre-TCO takeout availability at competitive terms indicates capital confidence in Chicago/Midwest residential fundamentals. Fast close (30 days) suggests streamlined underwriting and robust demand for lease-up financing. Relevant for developers in Chicago metro: favorable financing environment for new supply; monitor Buffalo Grove and similar suburban markets for lease-up velocity and absorption as bellwether for regional market health.

stories.title: Skin Care Brand FaceGym to Open New Tribeca Location at 110 Reade Street
stories.excerpt: Time to face the music. FaceGym, a skin care brand that describes itself as a “facial fitness” studio, has inked a 10-year, 2,400-square-foot lease for a new Tribeca spot at 110 Reade Street, according to landlord broker Platinum Commercial. Founded in 2014 in London, FaceGym offers customers “facial workouts” and “combines muscle manipulation techniques” to provide lifting and sculpting services without surgery, according to its website. The brand has 15 locations globally, including four others in New York City on the Upper East Side, in NoHo and in Midtown. “The strongest retail brands today are making long-term investments in neighborhoods that complement their identity and where they can build lasting relationships with their customers,” Platinum Commercial’s Steven Evans, who repped landlord 110 Reade Property Owner LLC, said in a statement. “Tribeca has evolved into one of Manhattan’s premier destinations for luxury wellness, beauty and experiential retail, attracting brands that value authenticity, quality and community. FaceGym is an ideal addition to that ecosystem.” The asking rent was $110 per square foot. The new location is expected to open this month. Isaacs and Company represented the tenant, but the names of the brokers who represented the tenant were not immediately available. Built in 1861 near the corner of Reade Street and West Broadway, 110 Reade Street is a six-story, mixed-use residential property with ground-floor retail. Fitness studio Pure Barre was a former tenant in the retail space. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: FaceGym inks 10-year, 2,400 SF lease at 110 Reade Street, Tribeca, Manhattan; $1,000+ nightly rates.
Luxury wellness/beauty retail tenant; 15 global locations, 4 other NYC locations (UES, NoHo, Midtown).
Tribeca positioning as prime luxury wellness and experiential retail destination.
stories.summary: FaceGym, a luxury facial fitness studio founded in London in 2014, has leased 2,400 square feet at 110 Reade Street in Tribeca for a 10-year term. The brand, which offers facial manipulation and sculpting services, operates 15 locations globally, including four other NYC locations. The Tribeca location signals the neighborhood's evolution as a premier destination for luxury wellness and experiential retail.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. Signals strong retail/experiential capital confidence in Tribeca's ultra-premium market positioning, but retail leasing does not indicate residential demand or supply shifts. However, sustained luxury brand migration to Tribeca (wellness, beauty) reflects affluent resident base and may support premium-tier residential rents in adjacent buildings; monitor Tribeca multifamily asking rents for continued upward pressure.

stories.title: SMBC Refis Apartments Near Dallas, Philly With $108M Loan
stories.excerpt: The Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys are longtime fierce rivals in the National Football League’s NFC East, but the two markets have a common link in one of commercial real estate’s latest multifamily financings. Ares Real Estate has inked a $107.5 million loan to refinance an apartment portfolio in the Dallas-Fort Worth and Philadelphia areas that together include nearly 600 units, Commercial Observer can first report. Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC) provided the loan for Ares’ Axis 110 property in Richardson, Texas, and for Skye 750 in King of Prussia, Pa. CBRE arranged the transaction with a global institutional debt advisory group consisting of Tom Traynor, Tom Rugg, Peter Griesinger, Arman Samouk and Kayla Kaloostian. The 2017-built Axis 110 at 110 W CityLine Drive in Richardson has 351 apartments next to the Dallas Area Rapid Transit CityLine Station. Resident amenities include a swimming pool, a skyline terrace, a fitness center and 8,110 square feet of ground-floor retail. Skye 750, at 750 Moore Road 20 miles northwest from Philadelphia, was completed in 2019 with 248 units. Its amenities include a swimming pool, a fire pit, a dog park, coworking space, a health club and a sauna. SMBC did not immediately return a request for comment. Ares declined to comment Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: SMBC provides $107.5M loan to refinance Ares Real Estate portfolio: ~600 units in Dallas-Fort Worth and Philadelphia.
Axis 110 (Richardson, Texas): 351 units, 2017-built, near DART CityLine Station; Skye 750 (King of Prussia, PA): separate facility.
Both properties feature ground-floor retail and transit accessibility; CBRE arranged transaction.
stories.summary: Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC) provided a $107.5 million loan to refinance Ares Real Estate's multifamily portfolio spanning two metros: Axis 110 in Richardson, Texas (351 units, 2017-built, near DART CityLine) and Skye 750 in King of Prussia, Pennsylvania, totaling nearly 600 units. CBRE arranged the transaction. Both properties are transit-accessible and feature ground-floor retail components.
stories.impact: Indicates stable financing availability for stabilized multifamily in secondary/suburban locations (Richardson, King of Prussia); SMBC appetite suggests moderate confidence in rental fundamentals across both DFW and Philly metros. Richardson near DART CityLine signals strong institutional focus on transit-oriented multifamily; developers should prioritize transit-proximate acquisitions and development in DFW suburbs, where job growth and in-migration support stable lease-up and occupancy in the 90%+ range.
